newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA JULY UNEMPLOYMENT FLAT AT 14.2 PCT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA JULY UNEMPLOYMENT FLAT AT 14.2 PCT.

text.p: Bulgaria's unemployment rate was virtually flat at 14.2 percent of workforce in July compared to June as the number of jobless rose by 1,766 people to 543,365, a National Labour Exchange (NLE) official said on Thursday.
"The number of jobless registered with us last month edged up only by 0.3 percent from June, which leaves the total percentage figure practically unchanged," an NLE official told Reuters.

Sustained demand for seasonal jobs in farming, tourism and the construction industry in July partly offset the effect of layoffs in state administration and the education and health sectors as Bulgaria entered the currency board, said the official.
The system, a form of IMF-prescribed restrictive fixed exchange rate regime, was introduced on July 1 to restore confidence in the lev currency, curb inflation and stabilise the economy.
Under the system the central bank is banned from lending to the government in order to boost financial discipline.

The unemployment rate was expected to rise in September as the government moves towards implementation of structural reforms agreed with multilateral lenders to close state loss-makers and cut red tape.
The World bank has approved a $25 million loan for severance payments and compensation for professional retraining and a further $80 million has been earmarked for lending to private entrepreneurs.
Bulgaria's 1996 average unemployment rate was 11.1 percent, down 0.3 points from 1995. Unemployment peaked in January 1994 when 16.6 percent of the workforce was jobless.
